section_summary: This section follows Japanese gold shipments, the expanding 1937 military budget, and American bank credits connected with trade in Japan and China. State Department officials and National City Bank examine how a possible Neutrality Act proclamation would affect outstanding letters of credit. The section also contains public inquiries about alleged American loans to Japan and replies distinguishing loans from ordinary commercial credits.

subfiles.title: Treasury inquiry about Japanese gold movements
subfiles.about: The Treasury Secretary suspects Japanese gold may be moving secretly through Europe.
subfiles.summary: Records a request for shipping inquiries and Feis's reservations about monitoring cargo unloading.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Tokyo about gold shipments
subfiles.about: The Department asks whether Japan is secretly sending gold through Italy or Germany.
subfiles.summary: Requests any embassy information bearing on untraced Japanese gold shipments.

subfiles.title: Conclusion of Tokyo telegram No. 454
subfiles.about: The Bank of Japan reports one September gold shipment to England and none to other countries.
subfiles.summary: Surviving closing page of the telegram; its paraphrase follows.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram No. 454
subfiles.about: The Bank of Japan gives figures for gold shipped to the United States and England.
subfiles.summary: Reports roughly 5.09 million ounces sent to the United States from March through October 4, with more possibly imminent. The vice governor denies shipments elsewhere except one to England.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of telegram No. 454
subfiles.about: Six copies of the Tokyo gold telegram paraphrase are forwarded.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the paraphrase to the Treasury.

subfiles.title: Further inquiry on Japanese gold exports
subfiles.about: Treasury seeks an estimate of further Japanese gold shipments before 1938.
subfiles.summary: Notes that October exports exceeded the bank vice governor's earlier figure and requests discreet follow-up.

subfiles.title: Legal analysis of National City Bank credits
subfiles.about: Hackworth analyzes how Neutrality Act proclamations could affect export letters of credit.
subfiles.summary: He reviews sections 1, 2 and 3 against National City Bank's existing commitments. Prohibited shipments would generally trigger the bank's contractual reservation, while section 3 might permit an exception for ordinary commercial credits. He notes that the bank's clause cites the superseded 1935 act.

subfiles.title: Foreign branches and section 3
subfiles.about: The memorandum considers whether section 3 applies to transactions at American banks' foreign branches.
subfiles.summary: It distinguishes branches' separate commercial dealings from parent bank control and cautions that specific transactions require individual examination.

subfiles.title: Murtaugh and Richardson branch deposit cases
subfiles.about: Two cases address where payment may be demanded on a bank branch deposit.
subfiles.summary: The cited decisions generally locate the primary payment obligation at the branch holding the deposit.

subfiles.title: Bluebird Undergarment Corporation v. Gomez
subfiles.about: A cited case treats a Puerto Rico branch deposit as located in Puerto Rico.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reproduces the court's reasoning that branches keep separate accounts and that a deposit is primarily payable where made. The New York attachment consequently failed.

subfiles.title: Chrzanowska and Pan-American branch cases
subfiles.about: Cited cases describe separate dealings between bank branches and their parent office.
subfiles.summary: The cases support treating branches as distinct business entities for checks, drafts and collection.

subfiles.title: Sokoloff v. National City Bank
subfiles.about: A cited case balances branch separateness against ultimate parent bank liability.
subfiles.summary: The case holds that branches conduct separate business but remain under parent control; closure of the Russian branch left the parent bank answerable.

subfiles.title: Request for legal review of bank questions
subfiles.about: Feis requests a legal examination of National City Bank's Neutrality Act questions.
subfiles.summary: Seeks departmental guidance and an expedited acknowledgment to the bank.

subfiles.title: Follow-up on foreign branch credits
subfiles.about: Feis asks whether section 3 reaches credits arranged through American banks' foreign branches.
subfiles.summary: Distinguishes transactions referred to New York from those completed by branches in China or Japan.

subfiles.title: Routing note on legal circulation
subfiles.about: A memorandum is to circulate for legal review after acknowledgment.
subfiles.summary: Calls for circulation and fuller examination of the bank's legal questions.

subfiles.title: Lancaster letter concerning outstanding credits, copy
subfiles.about: Lancaster forwards a technical memorandum about banks' credit obligations under a possible neutrality proclamation.
subfiles.summary: A poorly reproduced copy of the letter legibly reproduced on page 348.

subfiles.title: Irrevocable export letters of credit and the Neutrality Act
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: The memorandum assesses National City Bank's proposed protections for outstanding export credits.
subfiles.summary: It explains how a proclamation could leave the bank holding goods or facing claims under irrevocable letters of credit. It finds no apparent authority to delay the effective date and doubts that detailed contractual reservations belong in a proclamation. Further notes discuss bills of lading, competitive effects and the bank's saving clause.

subfiles.title: Routing note on legal circulation, copy
subfiles.about: A duplicate routing note requests circulation and legal examination.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the circulation instruction on page 335.

subfiles.title: Lancaster letter enclosing bank memorandum
subfiles.about: Lancaster raises concern that neutrality proclamations could disrupt outstanding bank credits.
subfiles.summary: Encloses an associate's technical memorandum for consideration if a proclamation becomes necessary.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to W. W. Lancaster on neutrality
subfiles.about: The bank describes civil and criminal risks to outstanding export credits under possible proclamations.
subfiles.summary: It examines arms restrictions, American ship restrictions and cash-and-carry rules. Through bills of lading and specially manufactured goods could magnify losses when shipments are stopped. The bank asks for time to adjust commitments or clearer reservations in proclamations.

subfiles.title: Irrevocable credit application
subfiles.to: National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: A sample form requests an irrevocable credit against shipping documents.
subfiles.summary: Blank application specifying drafts, insurance, bills of lading and applicant obligations.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Lancaster
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges the bank's letter and memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Says the Neutrality Act questions have been circulated for careful study.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to financing military operations
subfiles.about: The file note points to a report on financing Japanese operations in China.
subfiles.summary: References despatch No. 2584 in another file.

subfiles.title: Government finance extract
subfiles.about: An extract summarizes supplemental military budgets and temporary taxes.
subfiles.summary: Describes August appropriations, a tax increase and expected reliance on public loans.

subfiles.title: Senator Lodge's inquiry about banks financing Japan
subfiles.about: A constituent asks which two banks are financing Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests the banks' names.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Lodge
subfiles.about: The Department addresses an allegation that American banks finance Japan.
subfiles.summary: It knows of no financing beyond normal commercial credits and suggests asking Treasury.

subfiles.title: Shotwell telephone conversation
subfiles.about: Shotwell considers whether the United States might decline to buy Japanese gold.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck records Shotwell's suggestion and concern about the Far East, while noting uncertainty about exchange effects.

subfiles.title: National City Bank visit
subfiles.about: Rentschler and colleagues describe the bank's operations in Japan and China.
subfiles.summary: They offer cooperation with government policy; Feis notes that unusual long-term Japanese credits would attract comment.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Japanese financial capacity
subfiles.from: Ballantine; Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: The file note points to observations on Japan's ability to sustain operations in China.
subfiles.summary: References a memorandum filed under the Sino-Japanese conflict.

subfiles.title: Budget despatch annotation
subfiles.about: An officer highlights Tokyo's budget total and corrects its borrowing tabulation.
subfiles.summary: Notes ¥5.475 billion in authorized spending and an omitted special-accounts loan item.

subfiles.title: Japanese budget
subfiles.about: The embassy reviews Japanese appropriations and borrowing after fighting began in China.
subfiles.summary: Authorized general account spending reached ¥5.475 billion by September, including a ¥2.023 billion emergency military budget. The embassy expects further appropriations before the fiscal year ends. Its tabulation puts authorized general-account borrowing at ¥3.251 billion and notes that special accounts create further credit demands.

subfiles.title: Conversation with National City Bank officers
subfiles.about: Bank officers describe Japanese trade credits and offer to follow government policy.
subfiles.summary: Rentschler reports monthly import and export credit volumes, including machinery likely used in munitions. He says withdrawing the bank's services would hinder other banks' handling of those credits.

subfiles.title: Carroll inquiry about reported loans
subfiles.about: Carroll asks whether American banks are lending to Japan to finance war in China.
subfiles.summary: Questions whether the Department approved the reported loans.

subfiles.title: First reply to Carroll
subfiles.about: Hamilton explains that foreign bank loans need no State Department approval.
subfiles.summary: Suggests the reports concern short-term credits secured by Japanese gold in transit.

subfiles.title: Carroll's follow-up on bond policy
subfiles.about: Carroll asks whether the Department ended its policy of commenting on foreign bond issues.
subfiles.summary: Quotes a description of the policy in response to Hamilton's letter.

subfiles.title: Second reply to Carroll
subfiles.about: Feis distinguishes the former bond flotation policy from mandatory loan approval.
subfiles.summary: He explains that bankers were once invited to seek the Department's views on foreign bond issues, but that policy ended in 1933.

subfiles.title: Transmittal planning for embargo memoranda
subfiles.about: Two memoranda on an embargo and Japan's gold resources are proposed for transmission to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Records preparation of a covering instruction for both memoranda.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Bullitt-Sakoh conversation
subfiles.about: Sakoh predicts financial and economic collapse if the war continues six more months.
subfiles.summary: Points to Bullitt's conversation with the Japanese ambassador in Warsaw.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to September financial report
subfiles.about: The note points to a report on September financial conditions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: References embassy despatch No. 2624.

subfiles.title: September government finance extract
subfiles.about: The extract reports September budget totals and financial trends.
subfiles.summary: Notes the ¥5.475 billion budget, government gold purchases, an easy money market and the yen exchange rate.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram No. 531
subfiles.about: The Bank of Japan reports October and November gold exports and its yen policy.
subfiles.summary: October shipments to the United States totaled an estimated ¥138 million, and November shipments to date ¥60 million. The vice governor expects no more exports that year and reports no unusual yen weakness.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram No. 531
subfiles.about: The paraphrase restates the latest Japanese gold shipment figures.
subfiles.summary: It gives six October shipments and three November shipments, the last leaving Kobe on November 9. The vice governor says no further shipments are planned in 1937.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of telegram No. 531
subfiles.about: Six copies of the latest Tokyo gold telegram paraphrase are forwarded.
subfiles.summary: Forwards telegram No. 531 to Treasury.

subfiles.title: Goodrich letter opposing credits to Japan
subfiles.about: Goodrich urges the government to discourage reported American loans and credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Citing reports of development finance in Manchuria, he calls for withholding financial aid during Japanese aggression.

subfiles.title: Reply to Goodrich
subfiles.about: The Department responds to alleged American loans for development in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: It knows of no such recent loans and acknowledges Goodrich's views.
